feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical/strategic blend is compelling. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and could be tightened to improve impact, reduce duplication, and sharpen results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and specificity: examples like a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5M annual page views, and analytics stack expansion add substance.  
- Strong positioning: the profile and experience consistently present a rare mix of strategy, operations, content, and technical execution.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scale: include performance improvements, engagement gains, efficiency wins, revenue/support impact, or adoption results where possible.  
- Minor writing/style fixes: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the long channel list; “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” is enough given the rest of the CV.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel content, web, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective cross-functional communications. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “workflows and systems” overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are reinforced repeatedly in Work Experience and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital strategy & transformation” → “Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization.”
- Group related items and standardize style/plurals for parallel structure; e.g., “Editorial systems & workflow design,” “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Prioritize the most marketable/recent strengths tied to recent roles: web/CMS modernization, cross-channel leadership, analytics infrastructure, governance, and multimedia/event production.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance optimization • Digital operations & systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the summary.
- “Multi-channel communication” overlaps with both the header and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by emphasizing scope, outcomes, and the most senior/technical contributions.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Advised,” “Developed,” “Improved.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search success/engagement improvements, stakeholder groups served.
- Example rewrite: “Led AI-enabled search initiative across retrieval strategy, structured content design, and discovery UX; built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components; improved cross-channel governance, workflows, analytics, and CMS operations for large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level and leave technical detail to the project.
- Governance/analytics/workflows repeat prior NACo roles; focus this entry on what is new, current, or more advanced.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize business outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the most distinctive achievements without repeating channel management already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting cadence improvements, production volume, engagement growth, cost savings, or reduced vendor reliance from the in-house studio.
- Combine softer bullets for concision: merge analytics + governance into one results-oriented bullet tied to better reporting, publishing consistency, and cross-department planning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed as building new in-house studio capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and concrete outputs achieved at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague process bullets with stronger phrasing and metrics if available: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes spanning communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording tied to current work, e.g.:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- Use one consistent noun pattern across bullets; avoid mixing “leadership,” “planning,” and “messaging” styles.
- If space allows, make one item more differentiated, such as “Mission-driven digital communications strategy.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” substantially repeat the Core Competencies section.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague and partially duplicates experience bullets on storytelling, campaign platforms, and editorial coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work, not repeat every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older platforms unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, and consider removing jQuery, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages from this topline line.
- Use broader phrasing for seniority and relevance: replace “technical execution” with “platform delivery” or “web platforms & integrations.”
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost verbatim; Topline Skills should be shorter and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools after the capability terms: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and group related items: “Analytics infrastructure • KPI design • Executive dashboards/reporting • SEO & performance analysis • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity”
- If space allows elsewhere, add outcomes tied to recent work instead of here, e.g., improved reporting visibility, faster decision-making, or stronger optimization.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:

- “Leadership reporting” may be clearer as “executive reporting” or “executive dashboards.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and systems capability rather than basic task labels.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with more senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio system operation.”

items.title: University of Virginia

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS platforms or add light qualifiers that reflect actual depth.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency cues: **Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If Drupal is the clear flagship, lead with it and consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s not meaningful to target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the Topline section broader and use this item as a concise tools list only.
- Avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here since it already appears in Topline Skills and is evidenced in recent experience.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery  
- Add a second line for applied tooling: **Technical tooling:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/level wording such as “working knowledge” or “hands-on implementation” to signal practical use, not deep engineering specialization.
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may partially overlap with GitHub Actions; keep one section broader and this one tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation leadership. Since “workflow automation” and Airtable systems already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around systems used to run cross-team operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, replace one or two lower-value tools with a stronger qualifier: **Airtable workflow systems**, **cross-platform automation**, or **project intake/tracking**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to target roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership profile, but this line is too bare and misses the scale/enterprise context shown in recent NACo work. It should signal CRM/email operations strength without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Community Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier: **enterprise email operations**, **journey orchestration**, or **member communications platforms**.
- Best stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise email operations • Journey orchestration**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding newsletter audience size or campaign results here; those belong in recent work experience.
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and overlaps with core competencies; “CRM & Community Platforms” is clearer.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website traffic at the time, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience growth, email volume, or team size.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; specify what changed (e.g., publishing process, production cadence, turnaround time).
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize publishing workflows while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats governance/operations themes covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim generic phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace vague terms like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope tied to programs/policy support.
- Tighten into one impact-focused sentence or two short bullets; add outputs if known (episodes produced, stakeholders supported, research initiatives managed).
- Suggested rewrite: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams, while contributing digital and multimedia content for organizational communications. Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production planning and episode delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid overemphasizing broad digital/media duties here; save that narrative for the more senior, recent NACo roles.
